To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of an anchored primer in cDNA synthesis, a single-sided PCR prior to the RAGE-PCR and the optimization of dA-tailing conditions improve the efficiency of 5'-RAGE-PCR.
the 5'-RAGE-PCR method described here is a useful tool for the cloning and characterization of unknown 5'-and 3'-cDNAs and that this procedure is applicable to a wide range of different tissues.

we have optimized 5'- and RACE-PCR protocols by the use of an anchored dT-primer, single-sided PCR steps and the optimization of dA-tailing reactions to obtain the complete sequence of the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) kinase 6 ( GRK6) from rat brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of G-protein coupled receptor kinases and their role in receptor desensitization and signal transduction.
the molecular biology of signal transduction in the brain and the molecular mechanisms of learning and memory.
the molecular characterization of the rat brain cDNA clone GRK6 and the optimization of 5'-/3'RACE-PCR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RACE-PCR is a powerful method to determine the complete cDNA sequences of unknown genes and that the described protocol is an efficient method to perform RACE-PCR.
5'- and RACE-PCR is an easy-to-perform method for the cloning and sequencing of unknown cDNA termini.
RACE is an easy and fast way to obtain 5'- and/or 3'-cDNAs, but it is not a method for the isolation of complete cDNA sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5'- and the 3'-RACER protocol is a useful method to determine 100% of the cDNA sequence of a gene of interest within 2 days.
the method is a powerful tool to obtain cDNA sequences from small amounts of mRNA and to determine the 5' and/or 3' cDNA ends.
the method is an efficient tool to determine unknown cDNA termini and to identify different mRNA splice variants even in small amounts of tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RACE-PCR procedure can be improved to yield high-quality PCR products in a short time.
the 5'-/3'RACE-PCR method is not only a powerful tool to clone unknown 5'-/ 3'-cDNAs, but also to determine different transcription initiation sites or mRNA splice variants.
the RACE-PCR method should be used with care and the protocols should be optimized for the particular target cDNA.
